title: RemoteDocumentController has a batch mode that accumulates actions until push() and a streaming mode that pushes after each synchronous chain via queueMicrotask
content:
`RemoteDocumentController` composes a `PHDocumentController` and adds remote push/pull over GraphQL — for callers who want to create or edit documents and sync them to a reactor server **without** setting up a full `ReactorClient` (PGlite, job queue and the rest). It works with any controller from `PHDocumentController.forDocumentModel()`, and its action methods are type-safe and chainable.

Two modes:

**Batch.** Actions accumulate locally; `status.pendingActionCount` reports how many are waiting, and `push()` sends them in a **single `MutateDocument` call**.

```ts
controller.setName({ name: "A" });
controller.setName({ name: "B" });   // pendingActionCount === 2
await controller.push();             // one mutation
```

**Streaming.** Actions are pushed automatically after each synchronous chain via `queueMicrotask`, so everything in one chain — one microtask — is **coalesced into a single push**. If a push fails, the actions stay in the tracker and are retried on the next action; `onPushError` is the reporting hook.

Creating a document is the same call with `documentId: ""` plus a `parentIdentifier` naming the drive; pulling an existing one passes its id.

Note the standing on this class: ADR 0002 catalogued its structural limits — no persistence, no offline model, no shared cache, imperative and non-reactive, and a reimplementation of sync on weaker primitives — and folded its responsibilities into `GraphQLReactorClient.execute`. It remains the documented low-level path.
